subject: Discovery recap: Observability + evals — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Smith <alice.smith@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability + evals — next steps

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points
- Regressions in model outputs are surfacing in production and are often only discovered by customers (no automated regression alerts).
- No standardized "golden prompt" sets or structured evals to catch quality regressions before rollout.
- Limited observability: dashboards for per-route latency/cost and per-model output quality are missing; tracing hooks to follow requests across ingestion -> model call -> postprocessing are partial.
- Rollout guardrails are manual today (ad-hoc canary + human review).

Current stack & constraints
- Primary inference currently on a managed third-party endpoint; latency-sensitive sync endpoints for clinical summarization.
- Data residency: PHI-sensitive content; need to confirm deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private) during procurement.
- Team is small (2 ML infra, 1 ML eng) so operational automation is high priority.

Success criteria for POC
- Detect regressions on the golden prompt set with >80% coverage of critical intents.
- Alerting latency < 5 minutes from detection to page.
- Maintain 95th percentile latency < 200ms for sync endpoints during POC traffic profile.
- False-positive rate for regression alerts < 5% (initial tolerance).

Requested observability / eval deliverables
- Dashboards: per-route latency/cost, token breakdown, per-model output-quality over time, alert rules view.
- Tracing hooks: request ids passed through ingestion -> model -> postprocess so we can correlate failures/latency.
- Golden prompt sets: canonical csv with intent mapping and expected output heuristics for regression detection.
- Regression alerts: signal definitions, thresholds, and escalation path plus a demo of the alert firing and triage.
- Rollout guardrails: canary policies, automatic rollback triggers based on eval regressions + manual approval step.

Attachments: I attached a short observability requirements doc that captures what we discussed (zenhealth-observability-reqs.pdf) and a starter golden prompt template (golden-prompts.csv).

Next steps
1) I’ll share the attachments and a Drive folder with an initial dashboard mock and the golden prompt template (attached).
2) Aditya will run a short technical workshop next week to walk through tracing hooks and the eval pipeline.
3) You (Alice) to share SSO/SAML contact and the best person to provide PHI/mask-scope requirements.
4) We’ll schedule a POC kickoff (propose Wed Jul 7, 10:00am PT).

If that looks right, I’ll send a calendar invite and Aditya will include a short agenda for the technical workshop.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — this is a great recap and captures everything we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

- For success criteria, by "coverage of critical intents" can you call out what you mean by coverage (e.g., percent of intents in golden set vs production distribution)? We want to make sure the metric is actionable.
- On regression alerting: what channels does Redwood support for alerts (PagerDuty, email, Slack)? We’ll want PD for on-call and Slack for engineering.

We’re also keen to see an example dashboard and the tracing approach. Can you also include a rough timeline for a 4–6 week POC and an estimate for what Dedicated vs Private would look like cost-wise (ballpark ranges)?

I’ve attached our internal security contact (bob.chen@zenhealth.com) for initial SOC2/questionnaire triage — they’ll likely follow up with a standard security checklist.

Thanks — I’ll look for the invite for Jul 7.

Best,
Alice

Great questions, Alice — answering inline and adding a couple of concrete next steps below.

Coverage definition
- By coverage we mean percent of high-priority intents that are represented in the golden prompt set relative to the set of intents we observe in your production traffic. For POC we typically target the top ~20 critical intents (by traffic & business impact) and iterate. We’ll include a coverage dashboard that shows size of golden set vs production intent distribution.

Alerting channels
- Redwood supports PagerDuty, Slack, email, and webhook integrations for alerts. For PagerDuty we can send incidents when a regression alert fires; Slack for noisy engineering channels. We’ll confirm desired routing during the kickoff.

POC timeline & costs (rough)
- 4–6 week POC: week 0 kickoff + instrumentation, week 1–2 ingest sample traffic + build golden set, week 3 automated evals + dashboarding, week 4 tuning and runbook.
- Ballpark: Dedicated trial nodes (reserved-equivalent) for the POC typically range $X–$Y/month depending on concurrency — I’ll pull a more specific estimate after we scope throughput. Private (on-prem) is higher due to packaging/support; happy to layout both options in the next email.

Next steps (concrete)
1) I’ve shared a Drive folder with: dashboard mock, golden-prompts.csv template, and the observability requirements doc:
   https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-zenhealth-observability
2) Proposed POC kickoff: Wed Jul 7, 10:00am PT — I’ll send a calendar invite pending your confirmation.
3) Aditya will lead a 60-min technical workshop to cover tracing hooks and eval pipeline; Monica will help scope the golden prompt intents.
4) Alice/Bob to share security contact and SSO/SAML owner (Bob — can you confirm the best contact?)

Attachments included: golden-prompts.csv, zenhealth-observability-reqs.pdf

If that all sounds good I’ll send the invite and Aditya will include a brief agenda.

Thanks,
